sources.title: ASEAN Cosmetic Documents, Appendix III - ASEAN Cosmetic Claims Guideline (version date 4 September 2007)
sources.note: The guideline states that its examples are not exhaustive and that it is not the final authority.

sources.title: DAON LAB product sheets, section 7 'Claims not approved for this product' (fictional brand policy)
sources.note: Brand policy for the demo. Not a regulation.

softening_guidance.source_ref: Appendix III, Section 3 (final note on modifiers)
softening_guidance.text: Claims can be softened, i.e. made less functional and more cosmetic in nature, by the use of modifiers.
examples_from_source: Helps to remove oil from skin
Reduces the shine of oily skin
Makes your skin feel less oily

rules.source_ref: Appendix III, Section 2.d (Product presentation of cosmetics)
rules.title: Presented as treating or preventing disease
rules.description: A cosmetic must not be presented as treating or preventing disease in human beings. This covers spoken claims made in the broadcast.
rules.say_instead_hint: Describe a cosmetic feel or look, e.g. 'It helps relieve the feeling of dryness.'

rules.source_ref: Appendix III, Section 2.e (Physiological effects of cosmetics)
rules.title: Permanent results or results without continued use
rules.description: Cosmetic effects are typically not permanent and require regular use to be maintained. Claims of permanent results are not cosmetic.
unacceptable_examples: Use it once and your skin is fixed for good.
rules.say_instead_hint: Add continued use, e.g. 'With regular use, it helps keep skin hydrated.'

rules.source_ref: Appendix III, Decision process step 5 (Non-cosmetic function)
rules.title: Restores, corrects or modifies physiological function
rules.description: A product that permanently restores, corrects or modifies physiological function by a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action is not a cosmetic.
unacceptable_examples: It repairs your skin at the cellular level.
rules.say_instead_hint: Describe how skin looks or feels, e.g. 'It helps skin look smoother and feel hydrated.'

rules.title: Prevents, reduces or reverses physiological changes of ageing
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: 'Prevents, reduces or reverses the physiological changes and degeneration conditions brought about by aging'.
rules.say_instead_hint: Use an approved look/feel claim, e.g. 'It helps reduce the look of fine dryness lines.' (ampoule) or 'It helps keep skin hydrated.' (cream)

rules.title: Removes scars
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: 'Removes scars'.
unacceptable_examples: Your scars will fade away completely.
rules.say_instead_hint: Avoid scar claims. Talk about hydration or how skin looks overall.

rules.title: Prevents, heals, treats or stops acne
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: 'Prevents, heals, treats or stops acne'.
rules.say_instead_hint: Avoid acne claims. Say who it suits, e.g. 'It has a lightweight texture that suits oily skin.'

rules.title: Cellulite, slimming, swelling or fat claims
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: treatment of cellulite, lose centimetres, reduces/controls swelling/oedema, removes/burns fat.

rules.title: Numbing effect
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: 'Numbing effect'. Not this rule: saying that skin may feel a mild, temporary tingling, with patch-test advice (approved product wording).
rules.say_instead_hint: Describe sensory feel only, e.g. 'It feels cool and light on the skin.'

rules.title: Fungicidal or virucidal action
rules.description: Listed as unacceptable for skin products: 'Fungicidal action', 'Virucidal action'.
unacceptable_examples: It kills viruses on your skin.

rules.source_ref: Appendix III, Section 2.d.vi (particular target of the marketing)
rules.title: Targets groups with, or vulnerable to, specific conditions
rules.description: Product presentation includes marketing aimed at population groups with, or particularly vulnerable to, specific diseases or adverse conditions. The product sheets also state the products were not specifically tested on pregnant or breastfeeding women. Not this rule: telling pregnant or breastfeeding viewers that the product was not specifically tested for them and that they should check with their doctor first (the approved answer).
unacceptable_examples: It is safe for pregnant women.
rules.say_instead_hint: Refer to the doctor, e.g. 'If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, please check with your doctor first.'

rules.source_ref: Product sheet, section 7, Claims not approved
rules.title: Comparative or superlative claims
rules.description: Brand policy forbids comparative or superlative claims such as 'the best moisturiser in Singapore'.
unacceptable_examples: This is the best moisturiser in Singapore.
It is stronger than any other ampoule.
rules.say_instead_hint: Describe this product's own approved benefit instead, e.g. 'It helps keep skin hydrated for up to 24 hours in our in-house test.'

rules.source_ref: Product sheet, section 7, Claims not approved
rules.title: Absolute safety claims
rules.description: Brand policy forbids 'completely safe for everyone' and similar absolute safety claims.
rules.say_instead_hint: Use the approved patch-test claim with its qualifier: 'Patch tested with no irritation reactions in our in-house test.'

rules.source_ref: Product sheet, section 7, Claims not approved
rules.title: Compared to a medicine or prescription product
rules.description: Brand policy forbids saying the product works like a medicine or prescription product.
unacceptable_examples: It works like a prescription cream.
It's basically medicine for your skin.

rules.source_ref: Product sheet (Deep Hydration Ampoule), section 7, Claims not approved
rules.title: Whitening or permanent colour change
rules.description: Brand policy forbids whitening claims and claims of permanently changing skin colour.
unacceptable_examples: Your skin tone will change permanently.
rules.say_instead_hint: Use: 'Helps skin look more radiant and even-toned with continued use.'

rules.source_ref: Product sheet, section 5 (in-house test results) and section 7 (claims marked *)
rules.title: Test result without 'in our in-house test'
rules.description: Brand policy: a number from a test or study (a percentage, a count of participants such as '0 of 32', or a measured time such as '24 hours') must be said together with 'in our in-house test' or 'in our in-house study'. Use this rule, not an ageing, physiological or superlative rule, when the only problem is the missing qualifier. Not this rule: a sentence that already says the result is from our own test ('in our in-house test', 'in our 48-hour patch test'), benefit wording without a test number ('it keeps skin hydrated'), a viewer's question read out, or a denial.
unacceptable_examples: Hydration goes up forty-five percent right after one use.
Zero out of thirty-two people reacted in the patch test.
It keeps your skin hydrated for twenty-four hours.
rules.say_instead_hint: Say the same result with 'in our in-house test'.
